match.reason: No bank point teaches how internet access changes people's use of local shops and services: the digital divide card covers uneven access, the services-across-borders card covers offshored call-centre work, and the Year 7 technology card is too shallow for Years 9 and 10.

draft.title: Digital technology and access to services
card: The internet lets people use many services from a distance. They can shop, bank, study, see a doctor and work online.
A person in a small town can book a video appointment with a specialist in a city. A student can study a course taught by a school or university far away.
This changes how people use local shops and services. Some people buy online instead of in town, so local shops may lose customers. Other shops may sell online to reach buyers further away.
Using these services needs a device and a reliable internet connection.
draft.remember: The internet brings services to people from a distance, which can change how they use local shops and services.

a.q: Sam lives in a small town and used to drive to the city for a specialist. Now he sees the specialist by video call. What has digital technology done?
opts: Let him reach a service without travelling to it
Moved the specialist to live in his town
Made the service free for everyone in his town
Stopped him from using any local services
a.why: A video call lets Sam use a city service from home, so he does not need to travel. It does not move the specialist or make the service free, and he may still use local services.
a.clue: What no longer has to happen for Sam to see the specialist?

b.q: More people in Leila's town now buy clothes online. What is the most likely effect on the town's clothing shop?
opts: It may lose customers, unless it also sells online
It will close, because online shopping always wins
It will gain customers, because shoppers need advice
It will not change, because online shopping is separate
b.why: Some shoppers buy online instead of in town, so the shop may lose sales. It could also sell online to reach buyers further away. The shop will not always close, because the effect depends on what the shop does.
b.clue: Think about where the shoppers are now spending their money.

a.best: Let him reach a service without travelling to it

b.best: It may lose customers, unless it also sells online

problems.detail: The right option is the only one hedged with 'may' and is the longest. The other three all say 'will', so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

'Unless it also sells online' implies that selling online prevents the loss of customers. The card only says some shops may sell online to reach buyers further away, and the why says the same. The option overstates this as a condition that avoids the loss.

check.summary: Question b's right answer stands out as the only hedged and longest option. Its 'unless it also sells online' also overstates the card, which says selling online reaches more distant buyers, not that it stops the loss of local customers.

b.q: More people in Leila's town now buy clothes online. What is the most likely effect on the town's clothing shop?
opts: It is likely to lose some local customers to online sellers
It is likely to gain customers from the online sellers
It is likely to see no change, as online sales are separate
It is likely to lose customers only from outside the town
b.why: People in Leila's town who buy online are spending money that might have gone to the local shop, so it is likely to lose some customers. Online sales are not separate: each online purchase can replace a trip to the town's shop.
b.clue: Where were these shoppers buying clothes before?
